newsitem.title: USA: Enron, Portland General agree in Oregon pact.
newsitem.headline: Enron, Portland General agree in Oregon pact.

text.p: Enron Corp and Portland General Corp said they reached an agreement in principle with the staff of the Oregon Public Utility Commission regarding their proposed merger.
The parties were drafting a stipulation and expected to finalise their agreement on April 29, the companies said. The next step was to present the pact to commissioners for their approval, they said.
On April 14, Enron revised the terms of its proposed $2.1 billion acquisition of Portland General by increasing benefits for customers and lowering the payout to Portland General shareholders.

Houston-based Enron said it would guarantee a $141 million rate cut for customers of Portland General Electric Co but lower the payout ratio to 0.9825-for-one from one-for-one at which shares would be paid to Portland shareholders.

The revision was made following Oregon Public Utility Commission's decision to recommend Enron's acquisition be denied unless the companies came up with rate reductions of at least $141 million for Portland's electric utility customers.
A Portland General shareholder vote to approve the revised merger agreement was set for June 24, the companies said.
